create.name: Ring of Bone Zendo
create.bio:
Set on the San Juan Ridge, Ring of Bone Zendo is a lay Zen community in the Sierra Nevada foothills of California that belongs to the Diamond Sangha lineage of Robert Aitken Rōshi. It grew out of sittings that the poet Gary Snyder began in 1970 with the volunteers building his family's house, after his own years of training at Daitoku-ji in Kyoto. The group took its name in 1974, in memory of Snyder's friend the poet Lew Welch, and moved into its own forest zendo beside a meadow in 1982. Its teacher is Nelson Foster, one of Aitken's first dharma heirs, who was authorised to teach independently in 1989 and later succeeded Aitken as head of the Diamond Sangha. He edited The Roaring Stream, an anthology of Chinese and Japanese masters, and published Storehouse of Treasures in 2024.

The sangha is small, run entirely by volunteers and governed by its members through consensus, with no residential programme. Sunday morning and Wednesday evening sittings run through most of the year with chanting and private interviews, newcomers are shown the forms by a member on their first visit, and sesshin of one to eight days are held through the year. Seasonal gatherings include Buddha's Birthday and a Founders' Day honouring the people behind the zendo.

courses.title: Weekly zazen
courses.description: Sittings at the forest zendo on Sunday mornings and Wednesday evenings, with chanting, four periods of zazen and, usually, private interviews with the teacher. First-time visitors are asked to get in touch beforehand so that a member can guide them in and show them the forms.

courses.title: Sesshin
courses.description: Full-time silent retreats at the zendo of one to eight days, led in the Diamond Sangha way with zazen, chanting, meals in the meditation hall and meetings with the teacher. Places are limited and booked through each event's coordinator; reduced fees can be discussed.

courses.title: Membership
courses.description: After a year of taking part, participants may join as associate, sustaining or core members, according to how often they sit, serve and attend sesshin and the monthly business meetings.

free_resources.title: Ring of Bone newsletters
free_resources.description: The sangha's seasonal newsletters, with the current issue and an archive of earlier ones, mixing practice reflections, stories, poems and news from the zendo.
